epics.title: Workspace and Local Development Foundation

items.title: Create the isolated pnpm workspace layout
items.description: Create a nested, self-contained workspace in an isolated template folder with a web application, an API application, a contracts package, a UI package, and a config package. The workspace has its own lockfile, scripts, and lint rules, and shares nothing with Apex's root workspace. Document placeholders for project name, package scope, service name, and database name.
definitionOfDone: The workspace contains the five members with working internal package links
Running Apex's root install, build, test, and lint commands produces the same results with and without the template folder
The template contains no Apex-specific code and no AWS, pipeline, or governance files
Replacement placeholders are listed in the template README
nonFunctionalRequirements: Installing and building the template must not modify any file outside its folder
Template files must pass Apex's existing formatting check or be excluded through an approved minimal ignore entry

items.title: Pin the toolchain and record a compatibility table
items.description: Pin the Node LTS and pnpm versions through Corepack, commit the lockfile, require frozen installs, and publish a compatibility table of approved stable versions for Express 5, React, Vite, MUI, Drizzle, TypeScript, and the test tools.
definitionOfDone: Node and pnpm versions are pinned and enforced by Corepack
A frozen install succeeds from a clean checkout and fails when the lockfile is out of date
The compatibility table lists every pinned framework and tool version
Every dependency version in the workspace appears in the lockfile
nonFunctionalRequirements: Installs must be reproducible from the lockfile alone

items.title: Create the shared config package
items.description: Provide shared TypeScript, lint, formatting, and test configuration that all workspace members extend, so rules change in one place.
definitionOfDone: Every workspace member extends the shared TypeScript configuration
Lint and format commands run across all members from the workspace root
A deliberate lint violation in any member fails the root lint command
Shared test configuration is consumed by the web and API applications
nonFunctionalRequirements: A rule change in the config package must apply to every member without per-member edits

items.title: Add typed environment validation and an example environment file
items.description: Validate every environment variable with Zod at startup for the API and for build-time web settings. Missing or invalid required values abort startup with a clear message. Provide an example environment file that lists every variable and contains no secrets.
definitionOfDone: Startup aborts with a clear error when a required variable is missing or malformed
The example environment file lists every variable and contains no secrets
Web build-time variables are validated separately from server variables and carry no secrets
Unit tests cover valid, missing, and malformed values
nonFunctionalRequirements: Error messages must name the variable and never print secret values

items.title: Add Docker Compose PostgreSQL and the stable local script surface
items.description: Provide a Docker Compose definition for local PostgreSQL and named scripts for running the web and API in development, so the same script names serve developers and Platform Engineering's pipeline.

Named scripts exist for install, build, check, test, run, migrate, and seed
The local database settings match the example environment file
The README documents each script and its purpose

epics.title: Data and API Contract Layer

items.title: Define the app_users schema and data-access module
items.description: Define the app_users table with a UUID primary key, a unique external identity subject, a display name, an optional email, a status, and created and updated timestamps. Wrap Drizzle in a data-access module with a small interface to find a profile by external subject, create it, and update it. Add no password, session, role, audit, or flag columns.
definitionOfDone: The schema defines the listed columns with a unique constraint on the external identity subject
The data-access module exposes find, create, and update operations by external subject
Integration tests against real PostgreSQL cover create, find, update, and unique-constraint failure
No other table is defined
nonFunctionalRequirements: The data-access module must be the only code that imports the Drizzle client for application queries
Constraint violations must surface as typed errors, not raw database errors

items.title: Add the reviewed SQL migration workflow and standalone migration command
items.description: Generate SQL migrations from schema changes, commit them with the schema change, and provide a standalone migration command that can run apart from the application process. The application never runs migrations or changes schema at startup. Document the forward-fix rollback policy and the ownership split.
definitionOfDone: The initial migration creates app_users and is committed
The migration command runs standalone and exits non-zero on failure
Application startup contains no schema-changing code
A validation script confirms the committed migrations match the Drizzle schema
Documentation states that the application repository owns migration files, Platform Engineering owns execution, and rollback is forward-only in production
nonFunctionalRequirements: Migrations must be re-runnable without error once applied
A failed migration must exit with a non-zero status

items.title: Add the synthetic seed command
items.description: Provide a seed command that inserts synthetic app_users rows for local development and tests. Seeds never use real names, emails, or identity subjects.
definitionOfDone: The seed command inserts clearly synthetic rows
Running the seed twice leaves the same rows
The seed refuses to run when the environment is production
A test confirms seed values use synthetic domains and names
nonFunctionalRequirements: Running the seed twice must not duplicate rows or fail

The drift check exits non-zero and shows the difference when the document is stale
Generation is deterministic across repeated runs
The committed document validates as OpenAPI 3.1

Every route definition declares the request ID header and its error responses
Pagination parameters define a default and a maximum page size
Documentation lists the conventions for new endpoints
nonFunctionalRequirements: Error definitions must never include identity values or stack traces

epics.title: Reference API and Platform Services

items.title: Define the principal contract, adapter interface, and authentication middleware
items.description: Define an authenticated-principal contract carrying at least the external identity subject, an adapter interface that resolves a principal from a request, and an authentication middleware that rejects unauthenticated requests with a Problem Details 401. Swapping the adapter must need no change to route handlers

items.title: Build the Express composition root and error handling

businessRules.rule: The profile endpoints read or update only the profile of the authenticated principal, using the external subject supplied by the identity-provider adapter. No endpoint lists users, looks up another user, or accepts another user's identifier.
The development identity adapter can be selected only when the authentication mode is development and the environment is not production. Production startup aborts if it is selected.
The template defines no roles, permissions, or authorization policy. Protected routes require authentication only, and RBAC is an explicit extension point.

Zod schemas in shared route definitions are the single source of truth for validation, types, and documentation. The OpenAPI 3.1 document is generated from them and committed, and the drift check fails when the committed document differs from the generated one.
Every error response uses RFC 9457 Problem Details and carries the request ID. Routes are versioned and resource-oriented, and pagination conventions are bounded.

The application never changes the database schema at startup. Schema changes ship as reviewed SQL migrations committed with the Drizzle schema change in the application repository. Platform Engineering runs them as a separate deployment step, and production rollback uses forward corrective migrations.
Seeds, fixtures, and tests use synthetic data only. Logs, telemetry, and API error bodies never contain identity values (display name, email, external identity subject).

The template contains no AWS infrastructure, pipeline definitions, ECS configuration, repository governance files, runtime AI dependencies, or Apex-specific code. It has its own lockfile and scripts and does not change Apex runtime behavior or Apex builds.
businessRules.appliesTo: Isolated pnpm Workspace and Pinned Toolchain (Feature)

businessRules.rule: Dependencies use organization-approved stable versions, pinned through Corepack and a committed lockfile with frozen installs, and listed in a compatibility table.
businessRules.appliesTo: Isolated pnpm Workspace and Pinned Toolchain (Feature)

businessRules.rule: A missing or invalid required environment value aborts startup with a clear error. Production secrets arrive only through environment variables, and the example environment file contains no secrets.
The feature-flag interface is provider-neutral. The template ships a local adapter and no vendor SDK.
Coverage floors are 80% for lines, functions, and statements and 75% for branches.

The quality manifest and NFR manifest define gates and targets but no execution tiers or schedule. Each consuming team decides when checks run. Each project supplies its own NFR targets, and example values are illustrative only.
The production container is defined once, built in stages, runs as a non-root user, and packages the API and the built web client. It makes no AWS or ECS assumptions.
The developer skill requires the api-contract skill for any endpoint work and the ui-standards skill for any screen work. The QA and integration skills read the quality manifest.

assumptionsMade: The accepted ADR "Build from prompt (single-prompt-build-orchestration)" is cited in the transcript, but its text was not available in the repository checkout. The five-role skill set, quality manifest, and immutable project references follow the transcript's summary of it and should be confirmed against the ADR.

Platform Engineering is not an Apex persona. Backlog stories map it to `Platform Admin`, the closest cross-project administrator persona. Template consumers and Apex-launched development agents map to `Developer`. People who use the sample profile screen map to `Authenticated User`. No new personas are introduced.

`GET /api/v1/me` creates the `app_users` row on first authenticated access from the principal's subject and display name. The identity provider owns identities and the sample has no create endpoint, so this is the only way a profile can come to exist. Confirm this behavior.

The production container packages the API and the built web client, and Express serves the built client from the same process. The template still produces independent web and API build artifacts, as the transcript requires.

Apex's root formatting check scans the whole repository. The template must conform to Apex's existing formatting rules, or the maintainers must approve a minimal ignore entry. Confirm which approach to use.

The transcript does not name the tools for OpenAPI generation, load testing, secret and vulnerability scanning, license checks, or SBOM generation. Implementation selects them from the organization-approved set and records them in the compatibility table.
Automated dependency-update configuration is left to Platform Engineering with the pipeline and repository governance, because the transcript assigned both to them.
The set of `status` values on `app_users` is not specified. Implementation chooses a small documented set.
Example NFR values (P95 under 500 ms at 50 concurrent users, 100,000 user rows) illustrate the manifest format only. They are not requirements or promises.
Unresolved decisions that the template leaves as extension points are: production identity provider, RBAC, data classification, NFR targets and test execution policy, and feature-flag provider.

implementationPhases.rationale: The workspace, pinned toolchain, shared configuration, and local database are the base every other package builds, tests, and runs on. Nothing else can be built or verified until they exist.

The app_users schema with its migrations, and the Zod-authoritative contracts package, define the data and API shapes that the backend, web client, tests, and skills all consume. They must exist before any handler, screen, or contract test is written.

The identity adapter, profile and health API, observability, and flag interface use the persistence and contracts from Phase 2. The web client needs a working profile API, and the test framework needs working endpoints to verify.
